title.narrative: Connecting Youth to Gainful Entrepreneurship

description.narrative: Objective 1: Increased market relevant skills for refugee and host community youth: Objective 2: Increased access to diverse financial products and services for refugee & host community youth Objective 3: Increased access to business services, markets and opportunities for refugee & host community youth:

The Y-Connect is a 25 months project (December 2024 – December 2026) funded by the Embassy of the Kingdom of Netherlands (EKN) and implemented by AVSI Foundation in Nakivale Settlement Isingiro District. The project aims to improve the income of 1,700 refugee and host community youth in Nakivale Refugee Settlement, Isingiro District in agribusiness using a multisectoral approach. This project will provide skilling to 1,000 youth Not in Employment Education and Training (NEET) and 600 youth in secondary schools over a period of 24 months. The project integrates a strong learning agenda in which additional 100 youth will be provided with start-up capital only (with no skills or mentorship provided) to research the effectiveness of skilling and mentorship in increasing employment and incomes.
This project targets 1,100 youth Not in Employment Education and Training (NEET) and 600 youth in secondary schools. Overall, 30% nationals, 70% refugees and 45% males, 55% females.

Output 1.3.1 Youth businesses coached and mentored

description.narrative: AVSI’s experience shows that the top four reasons listed for business failure are: lack of demand, rigid owners, inability to manage growth and poor accounting. The business success rate does not only depend on the market forces and entrepreneurship abilities but also on being able to access the right support and technical know-how at the right time. Business coaching is an ideal and tested approach to support small enterprises to grow. Business coaching is a tailored individual or group business mentorship provided by Business coaches and market actors to ensure that businesses remain functional and grow progressively. Coaching involves an ongoing relationship where a coach supports and motivates participants to use their existing knowledge and skills to make informed and realistic decisions and achieve specific objectives along their business journey. It is a personalized platform that uniquely addresses the needs of individual youth.

The project aimed to coach 1,400 youth businesses.

Overall, 210 youth were coached in the first cohort by year-end. This is below target because coaching was intentionally sequenced to follow capital distribution, which only occurred in November 2025.

title.narrative: Outcome 1.3: Increased access to business services, markets, and economic opportunities for refugee and host community youth

description.narrative: Inadequate Business Support Services still remains one of the limiting factors to the growth of SMEs. Providing BDS to SMEs is not commercially viable for providers, as most need long-term, tailored support. The BDS provision on offer is often inappropriate (light touch, short-term) resulting in low success rates. To achieve, the project will offer a wide range of non-financial services for a period of 9 months to help entrepreneurs improve performance of their businesses, access markets, and enhance their ability to compete.

title.narrative: Output 1.2.1: Self-financing mechanisms strengthened

description.narrative: This output aims to ensure sustainable access to finance facilitating meaningful investment in sustainable livelihoods. Villages Savings and Loans Associations (VSLAs) will be a platform for pooling resources, allowing individuals to access capital for investment. The VSLA is a collective savings mechanism that fosters financial stability, expansion, and the establishment of new businesses, enhancing resilience within communities while promoting peer-to-peer learning, solidarity, trust, mutual support, and social cohesion. VSLA groups will also be used as a platform to reinforce financial management and business skills training by business coaches

title.narrative: OP Ind 1.2.1d: Average savings per month Per youth

description.narrative: This indicator measures the average monthly savings per youth across active VSLA groups, tracking savings discipline and the financial capacity of youth to invest in their enterprises.

comment.narrative: At baseline, no VSLA groups existed and therefore no savings data was available.
The overall, target for average monthly savings per youth was UGX 45,000. The target for Nationals (50,000) is slightly higher than Refugees (40000)

The monthly savings trend shows a pattern consistent with entrepreneurial behaviour: savings built through Q3, dipped in November as youth invested start-up capital into enterprise inputs, and recovered in December as first sales cycles completed. The December recovery saw refugee savings increase 40% above their September peak, confirming that savings discipline is now integrated into enterprise operations.

title.narrative: Outcome 1.2: Increased access to diverse financial products and services for refugee and host community youth

description.narrative: This result focuses on whether Y Connect youth are moving beyond savings into broader financial engagement, measured across two indicators that capture different depths of financial access. The first indicator measures reach: any youth who attempted to access a financial service, whether or not the attempt resulted in use. The second indicator measures uptake with purpose: the micro, small, and medium enterprises started by programme youth that actually obtained financial services to support their business activities. Together, the two indicators map the financial inclusion journey from first contact with a financial product through to sustained business finance.

title.narrative: Output 1.3.2: Youth linked to business opportunities and services

description.narrative: To ensure sustainable access to business support Services, the project will support youth MEs with business development services to assist them in improving their systems and technical capacities around planning and management, based on business skills gaps identified during the business assessment conducted throughout the mentorship process. AVSI will ensure that MEs are linked to appropriate and available BDS in marketing, planning, and financial management in addition to direct service delivery approach by business coaches. The blend of business coaches and private sector actors will ensure delivery of BDSs services for a sustained period of time. Further, they will provide non-financial market incentives for the private sector ensuring that they have ready market for their goods and services among the target participants and the wider community through facilitating sharing of market information related to their products and services
